guide.title: JSON to TypeScript guide

rules.title: How types are inferred
items: Strings, numbers and booleans become string, number and boolean. Numbers are always number, with no integer/float split.
A value that is only ever null becomes null; mixed with other values it becomes a union such as string | null.
In arrays of objects, keys present in only some items become optional (?), and differing value types are merged into a union.
Arrays collect their element types, e.g. number[] or (string | number)[]. An empty array becomes unknown[], and nested arrays become number[][].
An empty object {} has no known shape, so it becomes Record<string, unknown>.
Date-like values are still strings in JSON, so they stay string.

naming.title: How types are named
items: Nested objects get their own declaration named after the key in PascalCase: user_profile becomes UserProfile.
Array elements singularize simple English plurals: items becomes Item, categories becomes Category. Non-plural keys get an Item suffix, e.g. data becomes DataItem.

Name clashes get a number suffix such as User2. Built-in type names like Date, Record or Promise are avoided the same way, and with export off, browser (DOM) names like Location or Comment are avoided too so they do not merge with global declarations.
Objects with exactly the same shape are declared once and the name is reused.
Keys with hyphens or spaces, or starting with a digit, are quoted, e.g. "first-name".
A top-level array or primitive becomes a type alias such as type Root = Item[].

tips.title: Practical tips
items: For API responses, paste several records as an array rather than one. Keys missing in some records become optional, which is closer to the real response.
Cases missing from the sample cannot be inferred. Fields that only ever arrived as null need their real type written by hand (e.g. string | null).
TypeScript types are only checked at compile time. To be sure a server response really has this shape, validate it at runtime with a library such as zod or valibot.
Fields with a fixed set of values, like status, are more precise as literal unions such as 'active' | 'inactive'.
interface suits declaration merging and extends; type suits unions and intersections. Pick whichever matches your team convention.

guide.privacy: Everything runs in your browser. The JSON you paste is never sent to a server; only your last input is kept in this device's browser (localStorage) so you can pick up where you left off.

items.q: How do I convert JSON to a TypeScript interface?
items.a: Paste JSON into the input box and the interfaces are generated right away. Choose the root type name, interface or type, and export or readonly, then copy the result or download it as a .ts file.

items.q: Should I use interface or type?
items.a: For object shapes they are nearly identical. Interfaces merge when declared again under the same name and extend easily; type aliases are better for combining unions and intersections. A top-level array or primitive cannot be an interface, so it is always a type.

items.q: When is a field marked optional (?)?
items.a: When a key appears in only some items of an array of objects. A single object treats every key as required, so paste several records as an array if you want optional fields detected.

items.q: What type do null values get?
items.a: A value that is null in every sample becomes null; mixed with other values it becomes a union such as string | null. A null-only field has no known real type, so fix it by hand after converting.
JSON has no date or integer type, so dates stay string and all numbers become number. Change them to Date or a branded type after converting if you need to.

items.q: Is my JSON sent to a server?
items.a: No. Conversion runs only in your browser and nothing is uploaded. Only your last input is saved in this device's localStorage so you can continue on your next visit.

items.q: Why is no error position shown?
items.a: The position is read from the browser's error message. Chrome, Edge and Firefox usually report a line and column, but Safari gives no position, so only the message is shown. Common causes are trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys and comments.
